tagline: Build and automate the infrastructure software runs on in the cloud — provision with code, ship reliably.
what_you_do: You design, provision, and automate cloud infrastructure — spinning up networks, servers, and services with code instead of by hand, wiring up deployment pipelines, and keeping production healthy. It's powerful, in-demand work, but be honest with yourself: it's usually a second rung, not a first job. Most cloud engineers arrive from a support, systems, networking, or development background, then add cloud on top. This roadmap treats it as a destination and shows the on-ramp.
day_in_life: Write Terraform to provision a new environment instead of clicking through a console
Debug why a deployment pipeline failed and fix the automation so it can't happen again
Right-size resources to cut the monthly cloud bill without hurting performance
Respond to an alert that a service is degraded and trace it through logs and metrics
Review a teammate's infrastructure change before it reaches production

salary.entry: Reached via a first rung (support / sysadmin / dev), not day one
salary.note: No dedicated BLS code; figure approximates Computer Occupations, All Other (15-1299). Industry cloud-role averages skew higher and are self-selected. Treat as directional.

downsides: It's hard as a first job — most listings expect a prior rung plus cloud certs. DevOps/SRE work carries real on-call ('you build it, you run it'), the tool surface is sprawling, and you can be blamed for outages. Route in as a destination, not a starting point.

fits_if: You love automating repetitive work so you never do it by hand again
You're comfortable at the command line and want deep technical work
You want highly remote-friendly work and don't mind on-call
less_ideal_if: You're a complete beginner looking for a first IT job
You want lots of face-to-face customer interaction
You want to avoid coding and scripting

skills.name: Networking fundamentals
skills.note: Cloud is still networking — VPCs, subnets, and routing don't disappear.

skills.name: Scripting (Python / Bash)
skills.note: The automation force-multiplier at the heart of the role.

certs.title: Azure AZ-900 (Fundamentals)
certs.reason: A cheap, never-expiring first proof of cloud literacy — great orientation.

certs.title: AWS Cloud Practitioner
certs.reason: The AWS equivalent entry cert if your target employers are AWS shops.

certs.title: Azure AZ-104 (Administrator)
certs.reason: The associate-level admin cert that proves you can actually operate cloud infrastructure.

certs.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate
certs.reason: The high-signal AWS associate cert for designing real cloud systems.

trial.objective: Provision real infrastructure and deploy a page — the cloud loop end to end.
trial.disclosure: Free account (email) required on a cloud free tier; a local, no-account fallback is available to feel the serve-it-yourself half.

roadmap.title: Earn a first rung first
roadmap.focus: Cloud is rarely a first job. Get a support, systems, networking, or dev foundation — then cloud is a promotion, not a wall.

roadmap.title: Get cloud-literate
roadmap.focus: Learn Linux and cloud core concepts free on Microsoft Learn / AWS Skill Builder, then earn a fundamentals cert.

roadmap.title: Learn to operate the cloud
roadmap.focus: Study for an associate cert (AZ-104 or AWS SAA) and build a public infrastructure-as-code project — the real portfolio.

roadmap.title: Automate everything
roadmap.focus: Terraform, CI/CD, Docker, and Kubernetes. A public repo of automation is what turns a sysadmin into a cloud/platform engineer.

adjacent_paths.reason: A common on-ramp — networking is a prerequisite that carries straight into cloud networking.
Cloud security is a fast-growing crossover if you lean toward protection.
